title: The Declassified NASA File: 'We Saw a Ghost Galaxy That Collided With Ours'
hook: NASA declassified a file revealing a ghost galaxy that crashed into the Milky Way and left a trail of invisible stars, each one hiding a dark secret.
why_this_can_go_viral: Taps into forbidden knowledge of a hidden galactic event, with a threat that's already here but unseen.

title: The Asteroid That 'Eats' Sunlight—And It's Headed for Earth
hook: An asteroid that absorbs all light instead of reflecting it is silently barreling toward Earth, and we only spotted it by accident.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines an invisible predator with an imminent doomsday scenario, driving massive curiosity and fear.

title: The Dark Matter 'Sinkhole' That Swallowed a Star Whole
hook: A star vanished in seconds, pulled into a dark matter sinkhole that left no trace—except a gravitational scream we still can't explain.
why_this_can_go_viral: Makes dark matter personal and violent, with a terrifyingly quick destruction that feels like a cosmic horror story.

title: The Declassified KGB File: 'We Sent a Message to a Dead Planet—Something Answered'
hook: A declassified KGB file reveals they transmitted a signal to a dead planet, and the reply came back in a language that didn't exist before.
why_this_can_go_viral: Secret Soviet communication with the dead, plus an unknown response, creates a perfect conspiracy-espionage-horror mix.

title: The Stellar Danger: A Sun That 'Spits' Fireballs That Travel at 1% the Speed of Light
hook: A nearby star spits plasma fireballs traveling at 1% the speed of light, each one capable of punching through our solar system's defenses.
why_this_can_go_viral: High-speed cosmic bullets that ignore our shields—a visceral, action-movie-level stellar danger.

title: The Strange Cosmic Signal That 'Whispers' Our Own Names—Backward
hook: A signal from deep space whispers our own names backward, and every time we decode it, the message gets more personal.
why_this_can_go_viral: Eerily personal invasion of identity; viewers will immediately wonder what their name sounds like reversed.

title: The Rogue Planet That 'Wanders' With a Moon That Glows Like an Eye
hook: A rogue planet without a sun wanders the void, carrying a moon that glows with its own light—like a cosmic eye watching us.
why_this_can_go_viral: Eerie imagery of a self-illuminated moon triggers superstition and mystery, perfect for immersive storytelling.

title: The Extinction Event That 'Burned' the Atmosphere—Oxygen Levels Dropped to 5%
hook: A cosmic burn event set the atmosphere on fire, dropping oxygen to 5% and nearly extinguishing all complex life—and the trigger still orbits us.
why_this_can_go_viral: A sky-on-fire apocalypse that nearly killed everything, with a lingering threat that's still nearby.

title: The Dark Matter 'Needle' That Pierced a Galaxy—And Left a Scar
hook: A thin needle of dark matter pierced a galaxy, leaving a scar that's still bleeding dark energy—and the needle is pointed toward us.
why_this_can_go_viral: Imagery of a piercing weapon in space aimed at Earth triggers paranoia and fascination with cosmic destruction.

title: The Declassified NSA File: 'We Decoded a Signal—It Was a Map of Our Solar System'
hook: The NSA declassified a file showing a decoded alien signal that was a perfect map of our solar system, except one planet was highlighted in red.
why_this_can_go_viral: A treasure map from aliens with a terrifying target marker; viewers will obsess over which planet is highlighted.

title: The Stellar Danger: A Star That 'Bursts' Every 114 Days—And Its Radiation Reaches Us
hook: A star 50 light-years away explodes every 114 days like clockwork, and its radiation wave washes over Earth—we just never notice it.
why_this_can_go_viral: A predictable, recurring stellar event that silently bathes Earth in radiation—disruptive and unnerving.

title: The Strange Cosmic Signal That 'Counts' Prime Numbers—Then Stops Mid-Sequence
hook: A signal counts prime numbers perfectly for 10 minutes, then stops mid-sequence—as if something realized we were listening.
why_this_can_go_viral: The signal's sudden stop implies self-awareness, making viewers feel watched and hunted.

title: The Astronomical Anomaly: A Galaxy That 'Breathes'—Expanding and Contracting Every 200 Million Years
hook: A galaxy pulses like a living lung, expanding and contracting every 200 million years, and each breath churns out new dark matter.
why_this_can_go_viral: A cosmos that behaves like a living organism sparks awe, fear, and deep curiosity about what else is 'alive' out there.

title: The Fermi Paradox Answer: They're 'Dormant'—Waiting for the Universe to Cool Down
hook: Aliens aren't gone—they're hibernating in cold pockets, waiting for the universe to cool down so they can wake up and claim everything.
why_this_can_go_viral: Makes the silence terrifying—they're not dead, just waiting. Builds a countdown tension for when they wake.

title: The Rogue Planet That 'Pulls' Comets Into a Collision Course With Earth
hook: A hidden rogue planet beyond Neptune is steering comets directly toward Earth, like a cosmic sniper lining up shots.
why_this_can_go_viral: A planetary assassin hiding in the dark, redirecting comets—feels like a deliberate attack scheme.

title: The Declassified Soviet File: 'We Detected a Black Hole That's Eating Dark Energy'
hook: A Soviet file reveals a black hole that consumes dark energy instead of matter, growing faster than any known black hole—and it's coming this way.
why_this_can_go_viral: A black hole that breaks physics and is on a collision course—adds the mystery of a Soviet-era secret.

title: The Dark Matter 'Cocoon' That's Blanketing a Dead Star
hook: A dead star is wrapped in a dark matter cocoon, and inside, something is causing it to pulse with life again—like a cosmic resurrection.
why_this_can_go_viral: Resurrection of a dead star through dark matter feels like a zombie apocalypse on a cosmic scale.

title: The Strange Cosmic Signal That 'Comes' From a Star That Died 10,000 Years Ago
hook: We're receiving a signal from a star that went extinct 10,000 years ago—as if something is using its corpse as a radio tower.
why_this_can_go_viral: A message from a dead star implies a ghost or a usurper—creates a spooky, unsolved mystery that begs for answers.

title: The Extinction Event That 'Shook' the Earth From the Inside—A Crust Crack That Never Healed
hook: A cosmic impact cracked Earth's crust so deeply that it never healed, and magma still leaks from the wound—the crack is growing.
why_this_can_go_viral: Visual of an unhealed planetary scar that's spreading—feels like Earth is bleeding out from an ancient wound.

title: The Declassified CIA File: 'We Found a Satellite That Wasn't Ours—It Was Older Than Earth'
hook: The CIA declassified a file about a satellite found in orbit that predates Earth itself, carved with symbols that match no known civilization.
why_this_can_go_viral: An artifact older than Earth itself floating above us—instantly debunks history and ignites conspiracy theories.

title: The Stellar Danger: A Star That 'Winks'—And Every Wink Kills a Planet
hook: A star winks every 33 years, and each wink unleashed a gamma ray burst that sterilizes a nearby planet—its next wink points at us.
why_this_can_go_viral: A playful cosmic 'wink' that means death—creates a cruel, ironic horror that's highly shareable.

title: The Astronomical Anomaly: A Nebula That 'Screams' at 1,000 Decibels
hook: A nebula is screaming at 1,000 decibels, a sound so powerful it could shred matter—and the scream is getting louder every year.
why_this_can_go_viral: Space silence is terrifying—a screaming nebula that's ramping up is both surreal and threatening.
